key_insight: Coding agents can potentially automate parts of generalized task and motion planning by synthesizing the TAMP-specific code and heuristics that are usually hand-engineered. This could make it easier to transfer planning capability across many new instances without rebuilding the planner from scratch.
problem_solved: The paper addresses generalized task and motion planning (TAMP), where an agent must make discrete task decisions while also satisfying geometric, kinematic, and dynamic constraints. Existing approaches often require substantial domain-specific engineering to handle each new problem family.
method: Investigate whether coding agents can generate the planning components needed for generalized TAMP.
Use code synthesis to automate TAMP-specific engineering that is typically manual and time-consuming.
Evaluate how well the agent-produced planning artifacts exploit regularities across problem instances to reduce planning effort on new tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a path toward more scalable planning systems that are easier to adapt to new robotic or embodied environments. If successful, coding agents could lower the barrier to deploying TAMP in real-world settings by reducing expert hand-coding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: problem instance -> coding agent -> synthesized planner components -> solved TAMP task
Side-by-side comparison of manual TAMP engineering vs. agent-generated code

A chart showing reduced engineering effort or improved generalization across instances
paper_title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
paper_authors: Matteo Merler, Bowen Li, Josh Roy, Yichao Liang, Qianwei Wang
